# Rules and decisions in plain words (generated; do not edit)

Each line gives a rule or decision first, then its status and source with page, then the conditions under which it holds, and the row id in small text for lookup. A lead is a rule or suggestion without results of its own; worked and failed rows cite a paper, a measurement or a CHEPTA run. This page is for people and grows with every row: agents keep using problems.md and `python scripts/kb.py query`, which stay short. A struck-through line was corrected by the row named after it and no longer counts.

### azeotropic distillation: no convergence

- **Estimate the recycle and top products from an overall mass balance first: pure bottom products, a top vapour at the lowest-boiling heteroazeotrope, and a decanter splitting it into its two liquids with the solvent-lean liquid recycled.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 2.2, p. 7 (steps 2-3, Fig. 3b-c). When: heteroazeotropic distillation, initialisation, two column decanter. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.mass-balance-estimate-of-recycle</sub>
- **Initialise the heteroazeotropic column with a piecewise-linear composition profile joining the lowest-boiling heteroazeotrope, the saddle of its distillation region and the bottom product. Then check phases on each stage before solving the full column.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 2.2, p. 7 (step 5, Fig. 3e); Section 3.1.1, pp. 10-11 (Fig. 5). When: heteroazeotropic distillation, initialisation. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.piecewise-initial-profile</sub>
- **For a gradient-based solver, a three-phase stage can be treated as a quasi vapour-liquid stage on the overall liquid, with the two-liquid split done only inside the property call. This avoids discontinuities as stages switch between one and two liquids.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 2.1, pp. 4-5. When: heteroazeotropic distillation, equation oriented, phase transition. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.quasi-vle-for-three-phase-stages</sub>
- **When scanning feed composition widely, do not reuse one initialisation: the required stage numbers vary a lot, so re-initialise for each interval of feed composition.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 3.2.2, p. 16. When: heteroazeotropic distillation, feed composition scan. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.reinitialise-for-feed-changes</sub>
- **Even one heteroazeotropic column is hard to simulate: it can have multiple steady states and its products are very sensitive to the organic reflux. Luyben's careful manual start of ethanol dehydration still ended unconverged (as cited).** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 1, p. 2 (ref. 11). When: heteroazeotropic distillation, multiple steady states, cited example. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.single-column-already-hard</sub>
- **In the 1,4-dioxane and benzene case the optimisation relied on a small purge (0.8% of the feed), which the authors link to a poorer initial profile estimate.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 3.3, p. 16. When: heteroazeotropic distillation, purge, dioxane benzene case. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.small-purge-aids-robustness</sub>
- **Before setting up a heteroazeotropic column, compute and classify every azeotrope (nodes and saddles). The singular points show which profiles a column can reach at total reflux and guide the starting profile.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 2.2, pp. 5-7 (step 1, Figs. 2-3). When: heteroazeotropic distillation, initialisation, residue curve topology. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.topology-first</sub>

### azeotropic distillation: purity short

- **A converged design that sits well off the trend can be a poor local optimum. Small changes of the initial feed stage or total stage number removed such outliers.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 3.1.2, p. 12; Section 3.3.1, p. 17. When: heteroazeotropic distillation, optimisation, local optimum. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.outliers-from-integer-fixing</sub>

When: heteroazeotropic distillation, phase stability. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.phase-stability-every-stage</sub>

### reactive distillation: purity short

- **A reactive column for ethylene glycol can have several steady states, one of which accumulates ethylene oxide at the top. A converged run that misses the glycol target may be on the wrong one.** lead, book or review; Othman 2024, Introduction, p. 2 (citing earlier modelling studies). When: non catalytic, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>othman-2024-meg-reactive-distillation.rd-multiple-steady-states-oxide-overhead</sub>
- **Reactive columns often have several steady states for the same inputs; find them by scanning a parameter or restarting from different initial estimates before accepting one.** lead, book or review; Steffen et al. 2024, Initial estimates, p. 22. When: multiple steady states, bears on ethylene glycol, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>steffen-2024-rd-modelling-review.multiple-steady-states</sub>

### reactive distillation: slow

- **Homotopy continuation does not need good starting values but costs much more computation, because the modified system is solved many times; Newton or Broyden from good estimates is the better default.** lead, book or review; Steffen et al. 2024, Numerical methods, p. 18; Initial estimates, pp. 22-23. When: homotopy, bears on ethylene glycol, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>steffen-2024-rd-modelling-review.homotopy-robust-but-costly</sub>

- **The paper models glycol + water with the cubic-plus-association (CPA) equation of state, chosen for associating glycol and water, and checks for liquid phase splitting on the stages.** lead, book or review; Othman 2024, Model, p. 3. When: property method, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>othman-2024-meg-reactive-distillation.cpa-for-glycol-water</sub>

## General design rules by operation

### absorber column

- **Size the diameter of packed absorbers and strippers for 60 to 80% of their flooding capacity, and the packed height from earlier studies or a height-to-diameter ratio.** lead, book or review; Palomar et al. 2024, Section 'Methodology for Applying Process Simulations': operation unit design. When: packed column, sizing. <sub>palomar-2024-il-process-simulation.packed-column-capacity</sub>
- **When a regeneration column runs under vacuum, count the energy to compress its vapour back to atmospheric pressure in the utility demand.** lead, book or review; Palomar et al. 2024, Section 'Methodology for Applying Process Simulations': process modelling and simulations. When: vacuum, regeneration, utilities. <sub>palomar-2024-il-process-simulation.vacuum-energy-counted</sub>

### azeotropic distillation

- **Removing water azeotropically during esterification shortens the reaction and raises conversion; a cited isoamyl acetate study reports 2.7% higher conversion than ordinary water separation.** lead, book or review; Guo & Wang 2019, Section 2.3, p. 337. When: esterification, cited example, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>guo-wang-2019-azeotropic-distillation.azeotropic-water-removal-in-esterification</sub>
- **Prefer an entrainer that forms two liquid phases with the mixture, so a decanter separates and returns it; homogeneous azeotropic distillation recirculates more azeotrope and uses more energy.** lead, book or review; Guo & Wang 2019, Section 1, p. 334. When: entrainer choice, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>guo-wang-2019-azeotropic-distillation.prefer-heterogeneous-entrainer</sub>
- **For dehydrating a 6 mol% ethanol broth, cyclohexane and hexane gave the same annual cost within estimate accuracy, while isooctane and toluene cost over 15% more. Solvent make-up was below 0.4% of cost.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 3.1.1, pp. 9-10 (Fig. 4). When: heteroazeotropic distillation, solvent screening, 6 mol percent feed, atmospheric. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.ethanol-solvent-screen</sub>
- **Nearly all Pareto-optimal designs fell within 5% of the minimum annual cost while capital and operating cost could shift by about 20%, leaving freedom between larger columns and lower energy.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 3.1.2, p. 11 (Fig. 6); Section 3.2.1, p. 14 (Fig. 9). When: heteroazeotropic distillation, multi objective, conceptual design. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.flat-cost-optimum</sub>
- **A heterogeneous azeotrope is a prerequisite for heteroazeotropic distillation and is always minimum-boiling. The usual process pairs a simple column and a heteroazeotropic column with a decanter, each giving one product as bottoms.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 1, p. 1; Section 2.1, p. 4 (Fig. 1). When: heteroazeotropic distillation, two column decanter. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.heteroazeotrope-prerequisite</sub>
- **The 1,4-dioxane case's cost falls almost linearly with feed concentration, unlike the other two cases. The authors conclude that pre-concentration must be judged case by case, not by a heuristic.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 3.3.2, p. 18 (Fig. 13). When: heteroazeotropic distillation, feed composition scan. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.no-general-preconcentration-heuristic</sub>
- **For ethanol dehydration the specific cost falls steeply up to about 20 mol% ethanol in the feed and then flattens, so pre-concentrating a dilute feed to about 20 mol% may pay. For an ethyl acetate feed already in the flat region it would not.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 3.1.3, pp. 12-13 (Fig. 7); Section 3.2.2, p. 15 (Fig. 10). When: heteroazeotropic distillation, feed composition scan, preconcentration. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.preconcentrate-dilute-ethanol</sub>
- **Three ternary topologies cover most solvent-based heteroazeotropic separations (four, three or two azeotropes; about 26%, 8% and 21% of 1365 surveyed mixtures, as cited). Their complexity defeats simple solvent-selection indicators.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 1, p. 2; Section 2.2, p. 6 (Fig. 2). When: heteroazeotropic distillation, solvent screening, residue curve topology. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.three-common-topologies</sub>
- **Acetic acid and water form no azeotrope but are close-boiling, so heterogeneous azeotropic distillation is used; with n-butyl acetate as entrainer a cited study cut annual cost by 55% against plain distillation, and dilute feeds often add a preconcentrator column.** lead, book or review; Valentini & Vaccaro 2020, Section 2.2. When: acid dehydration, cited example, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>valentini-2020-azeotropes-waste.butyl-acetate-entrainer-for-acid-water</sub>
- **Screen heterogeneous entrainers by the width of the miscibility gap, the composition of the azeotrope they form, and the temperature gaps to the other azeotropes in the system.** lead, book or review; Valentini & Vaccaro 2020, Section 2.2 (cited screening of 60 candidates). When: entrainer choice, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>valentini-2020-azeotropes-waste.entrainer-screening-criteria</sub>
- **Heterogeneous azeotropic distillation can be built as a dividing-wall column; a cited solvent-recovery case saved about 33% energy and 20% annual cost.** lead, book or review; Valentini & Vaccaro 2020, Section 2.2. When: dividing wall column, cited example. <sub>valentini-2020-azeotropes-waste.heteroazeotropic-dwc</sub>
- **For aqueous solvent mixtures with several azeotropes, hybrid extractive-heterogeneous azeotropic distillation uses the water already present as entrainer, so no new solvent or azeotrope is added.** lead, book or review; Valentini & Vaccaro 2020, Section 2.3. When: solvent recovery, multicomponent waste. <sub>valentini-2020-azeotropes-waste.water-as-auto-entrainer</sub>

### cstr

- **Homogeneous mineral-acid catalysts are active but corrode equipment, cannot be recovered and add purification steps. Solid acid catalysts avoid these drawbacks.** lead, book or review; Hoff & Eisenacher 2025, Sections 2.1 and 2.2. When: esterification, catalyst choice, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>hoff-eisenacher-2025-esterification-review.homogeneous-acid-drawbacks</sub>
- **Large plants run continuously; a single stirred tank does not reach batch productivity, but stirred tanks in series do.** lead, book or review; Pasha et al. 2021, Section 'Process design of biodiesel production using chemical catalyst'. When: large scale, continuous. <sub>pasha-2021-biodiesel-process-design.continuous-cstrs-in-series</sub>

### decanter

- **Condense the reactive column's overhead into a decanter, draw the water phase off as wastewater (about 102 kmol/h) and return the whole organic phase to the column as reflux.** lead, book or review; Al-Rabiah et al. 2022, Section 6.2, p. 15 (Fig. 16, Table 9 stream 3). When: reactive distillation overhead, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>al-rabiah-2022.rd-decanter-returns-organic</sub>
- **In the paper's reactive-distillation balance the wastewater carries about 1.5 kmol/h ester, 1.3 acid and 0.2 butanol per 100 kmol/h of each feed. The decanter's water phase, not the bottoms, is where most ester is lost.** lead, book or review; Al-Rabiah et al. 2022, Table 9, p. 15 (streams 3-4). When: reactive distillation overhead, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>al-rabiah-2022.rd-loss-in-water-phase</sub>
- **Split an alcohol-water heterogeneous azeotrope with a decanter and two strippers: the organic layer gives dry alcohol at the bottom of one, the aqueous layer gives water at the bottom of the other, and both overheads return to the decanter.** lead, book or review; Fu et al. 2021, Introduction (Fig. 1). When: alcohol water heteroazeotrope, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>fu-2021-isobutanol-recovery.decanter-with-two-strippers</sub>
- **In a cited acetic acid dehydration process, a partial condenser between the column top and the decanter stopped azeotrope building up in the column and cut energy use.** lead, book or review; Guo & Wang 2019, Section 2.2, p. 336. When: acid dehydration, cited example, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>guo-wang-2019-azeotropic-distillation.partial-condenser-before-decanter</sub>
- **In conceptual design the decanter is often left uncosted because its size depends on a disengagement time that is not yet known.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 2.1, p. 5. When: heteroazeotropic distillation, conceptual design, costing. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.decanter-uncosted-in-concept</sub>
- **Reactors in series with decanters between them remove a heavy liquid product (glycerol) as it forms and allow a reactant to be added in stages.** lead, book or review; Pasha et al. 2021, Section 'Process design of biodiesel production using biocatalyst'. When: reactors in series, staged addition. <sub>pasha-2021-biodiesel-process-design.staged-decanting</sub>

### distillation

- **In both the conventional and the membrane-reactor balances about 1 kmol/h acetic acid (the small acid excess of the fresh feed) leaves with about 100 kmol/h ester in the bottoms, which sets the purity near 99 mol%.** lead, book or review; Al-Rabiah et al. 2022, Table 4, p. 9 (streams 1, 2, 6); Table 7, p. 14 (streams 1, 2, 6). When: product specification, conventional route, membrane route, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>al-rabiah-2022.acid-slip-sets-purity</sub>
- **n-Butanol and butyl acetate form an azeotrope at 101 kPa; the paper separates them at about 300 kPa, where the split is possible but needs many stages (42, feed on stage 21, reboiler 5.2 MW). When: elevated pressure, after membrane reactor, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>al-rabiah-2022.butanol-ester-split-at-pressure</sub>
- **The conventional route's medium-pressure steam (218,729 MWh/a) is about eight times that of reactive distillation and five times that of the membrane-reactor route, because of its three columns.** lead, book or review; Al-Rabiah et al. 2022, Section 7.1, p. 16 (Table 10). When: conventional route, utilities, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>al-rabiah-2022.conventional-steam-heavy</sub>
- **When the required purity is close to the feed composition, accepting a non-sharp split cuts reboiler duty substantially; do not design for sharper splits than needed.** lead, book or review; Blahušiak et al. 2018, Section 2.1, p. 304 (Fig. 4). When: purity target. <sub>blahusiak-2018-separation-selection.relax-purity</sub>
- **Between relative volatilities of about 1.3 and 10, distillation is the logical choice, and a solvent to raise volatility is worth considering only up to about 3. Below about 1.3 the minimum reflux rises steeply, so consider heat-pumped distillation or solvent-based separation.** lead, book or review; Blahušiak et al. 2018, Section 2.1, p. 304 (Figs. 2-3). When: technology choice. <sub>blahusiak-2018-separation-selection.volatility-ranges</sub>
- **Whether to recover a waste solvent by distillation or incinerate it depends on the energy embodied in making it: recovering tetrahydrofuran saves energy, while diethyl ether is better incinerated.** lead, book or review; Byrne et al. 2016, Recovery or incineration (ETH tool), p. 4. When: solvent recovery. <sub>byrne-2016-solvent-selection-guides.recover-or-incinerate</sub>
- **Lower the pressure of the columns whose split improves at lower pressure, keeping each condenser above ambient temperature; this raises relative volatility and widens temperature differences for heat integration.** lead, book or review; Chen et al. 2018, Methods: 'Decreasing the column pressure'. When: column pressure, heat integration. <sub>chen-2018-abe-distillation.lower-pressure-of-sensitive-columns</sub>
- **A dividing-wall column can match a two-column sequence's sharp ternary split with fewer trays, but with too few trays it needs much more reflux, and its liquid and vapour split ratios strongly affect the result.** lead, book or review; Henrique et al. 2020, Conclusions, p. 165. When: dividing wall column. <sub>henrique-2020-dwc-simulation.dwc-trays-reflux-splits</sub>
- **Most of the energy saving of a fully coupled (Petlyuk) arrangement comes from the prefractionator doing only a rough split, which avoids remixing; a dividing-wall column is its single-shell equivalent.** lead, book or review; Henrique et al. 2020, Introduction, p. 150. When: thermally coupled, dividing wall column. <sub>henrique-2020-dwc-simulation.prefractionator-avoids-remixing</sub>
- **After the first concentration step, take the most volatile product (acetone) first as distillate at 99.8 wt%, leaving isopropanol and water for the azeotrope steps.** lead, book or review; Janković et al. 2023, Results, Recovery of high-purity products, pp. 719-720. When: fermentation broth, sequence, atmospheric. <sub>jankovic-2023-ipa-acetone-recovery.acetone-first</sub>
- **When the broth holds live microorganisms, keep the first separation at the fermentation temperature (30 C) by vacuum distillation (condenser about 0.03 bar). The bottoms with cells and most water can then return to the fermenter.** lead, book or review; Janković et al. 2023, Methods, p. 715; Results, Vacuum distillation, p. 717. When: fermentation broth, vacuum, 30 c limit, cell recycle. <sub>jankovic-2023-ipa-acetone-recovery.cold-first-separation-for-live-cells</sub>
- **Recovering isopropanol and acetone from broth with over 94 wt% water took 1.3-2.0 kWh primary energy per kg product in the paper's designs; for the vacuum design it stays under 2 or 3 kWh/kg at 2.5 or 1.2 wt% products.** lead, book or review; Janković et al. 2023, Abstract, p. 714; Results, Sustainability metrics, p. 723 (Table 5). When: fermentation broth, about 5 wt percent products. <sub>jankovic-2023-ipa-acetone-recovery.dilute-energy-scale</sub>
- **At very low pressure the condenser falls below cooling-water temperature (about 10 C at 0.032 bar) and needs chilled water. Pass-through distillation avoids this by absorbing the vapour into LiBr brine and desorbing it at higher pressure.** lead, book or review; Janković et al. 2023, Results, Vacuum distillation, p. 717; Pass-through distillation, p. 718. When: fermentation broth, vacuum, pass through distillation, lithium bromide. <sub>jankovic-2023-ipa-acetone-recovery.vacuum-condenser-needs-chilled-water</sub>
- **A classic sequencing heuristic, reported by the authors, leaves the most difficult split to last because it needs a high reflux ratio.** lead, book or review; Li et al. 2023, Section 2, p. 5. When: sequencing. Disagrees with another row here. <sub>li-2023-distillation-sequences.hardest-split-last</sub>
- **The authors find the hardest split can also pay early, and that non-key components present during a difficult split inflate the column flows; the balance depends on the case, so sequences should be compared by optimisation.** lead, book or review; Li et al. 2023, Section 2, p. 5. When: sequencing. Disagrees with another row here. <sub>li-2023-distillation-sequences.hardest-split-not-always-last</sub>
- **Choose column pressure so the condenser can use cooling water rather than refrigeration, and set it together with heat integration.** lead, book or review; Li et al. 2023, Section 2, p. 5. When: column pressure, utilities. <sub>li-2023-distillation-sequences.pressure-for-cooling-water</sub>
- **Shortcut column models (Fenske-Underwood-Gilliland) combined with heat-exchanger network synthesis screened distillation sequences reliably; only the best few needed rigorous simulation.** lead, book or review; Li et al. 2023, Abstract, p. 1; Conclusions, p. 14. When: sequencing, screening. <sub>li-2023-distillation-sequences.shortcut-screening</sub>
- **Hydrolysing ethylene carbonate needs water close to stoichiometric and gives far fewer heavy glycols than direct hydration (1,532 versus 22,270 t/a in the paper's simulations). When: ethylene carbonate route, route choice, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>shehata-2024-meg-routes.carbonate-route-fewer-heavy-glycols</sub>
- **Operate the glycol dehydration and product columns under vacuum so the bottoms stay below the temperature at which the glycol degrades (170 C in the paper). The product glycol is drawn from the side and the heavier glycols leave at the bottom.** lead, book or review; Shehata et al. 2024, Section 'MEG production via direct EO hydration process', p. 8. When: vacuum, side draw, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>shehata-2024-meg-routes.vacuum-glycol-columns</sub>

- **Esterification of n-butanol with acetic acid is mildly exothermic (about -29 kJ/mol), so its equilibrium conversion falls as reaction temperature rises (the paper's Aspen equilibrium-reactor scan).** lead, book or review; Al-Rabiah et al. 2022, Section 2, pp. 2-3 (Eq. 1, Fig. 1); Section 6.1, p. 12 (Fig. 13). When: liquid phase, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>al-rabiah-2022.equilibrium-conversion-falls-with-temperature</sub>

### extraction

- **Acetic acid and water have low relative volatility and a tangent pinch at high acid purity, so solvent-based separations are preferred; in extractive or azeotropic distillation water leaves at the top because the acid is the heavy component.** lead, book or review; Blahušiak et al. 2018, Section 3.4, p. 316. When: acid recovery, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>blahusiak-2018-separation-selection.acetic-acid-water-solvent-based</sub>
- **Avoid plain distillation for strongly asymmetric feeds (one component dilute), where its internal efficiency is low; liquid-liquid extraction or extractive distillation are usually preferred.** lead, book or review; Blahušiak et al. 2018, Section 2.1, p. 304; Conclusions, p. 317. When: technology choice, asymmetric feed, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>blahusiak-2018-separation-selection.avoid-distillation-for-dilute-feeds</sub>
- **Low-boiling solvents such as ethyl acetate co-extract much water when recovering acetic acid, but their heterogeneous azeotrope with water splits on cooling, which cuts the regeneration duty.** lead, book or review; Blahušiak et al. 2018, Section 3.4, p. 316 (Fig. 20). When: acid recovery, solvent regeneration. <sub>blahusiak-2018-separation-selection.low-boiling-solvent-coextracts-water</sub>
- **Where an ether solvent is needed, 2-methyltetrahydrofuran and tert-butyl methyl ether are preferred to tetrahydrofuran and diethyl ether.** lead, book or review; Byrne et al. 2016, Unified guides, p. 9. When: solvent choice. <sub>byrne-2016-solvent-selection-guides.ether-substitutes</sub>
- **Across the Pfizer, GSK and Sanofi guides, water, n-propyl and isopropyl acetate and 1- and 2-butanol are rated green, while chlorinated solvents, NMP, DMF, DMAc, benzene, hexane, 1,4-dioxane and diethyl ether are undesirable.** lead, book or review; Byrne et al. 2016, Unified guides, pp. 8-9 (Figs. 6-7). When: solvent choice. <sub>byrne-2016-solvent-selection-guides.green-and-undesirable-solvents</sub>
- **Adding a strong salting-out salt (potassium carbonate) raised the alcohol's partition and dehydration with the salt staying in the aqueous phase, and salting-out plus distillation used less energy than solvent extraction.** lead, book or review; Fu et al. 2021, Concluding remarks. When: salting out. <sub>fu-2021-isobutanol-recovery.salting-out</sub>
- **Choose extractant boiling points so regeneration takes each one overhead or at the bottom without an extra column; a heavier biocompatible extractant cut the regeneration section from three columns to two.** lead, book or review; Díaz & Tost 2017, Methods: 'Extractant selection'. When: extractant choice, regeneration. <sub>grisales-2017-abe-extraction.extractant-boiling-for-fewer-columns</sub>
- **For recovery from a dilute product stream, the product concentration fed to separation (set by the upstream yield) dominates the energy needed per kilogram of product.** lead, book or review; Díaz & Tost 2017, Conclusions. When: energy per product. <sub>grisales-2017-abe-extraction.feed-concentration-dominates</sub>

### extractive distillation

- **The conventional route's stream table circulates about 440 kmol/h of 1,4-butanediol against about 186 kmol/h of first-column distillate (100 water, 43 butanol, 42 acid), roughly 2.4 mol solvent per mol (Lab's ratio).** lead, book or review; Al-Rabiah et al. 2022, Table 7, p. 14 (streams 5, 9, 13). When: conventional route, solvent 1 4 butanediol, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>al-rabiah-2022.conventional-extractive-with-butanediol</sub>
- **Choose a solvent boiling at least 50 C above the mixture so it forms no azeotrope in regeneration, and weigh selectivity above capacity.** lead, book or review; Blahušiak et al. 2018, Section 2.4, p. 311; Conclusions, p. 317. - **Dehydrate isopropanol by extractive distillation with ethylene glycol; a solvent-to-feed mass ratio of 1.1 minimised the energy of the extractive and solvent-recovery columns together.** lead, book or review; Janković et al. 2023, Results, Recovery of high-purity products, p. 720 (Fig. 5b). When: fermentation broth, solvent to feed, atmospheric. <sub>jankovic-2023-ipa-acetone-recovery.ethylene-glycol-solvent-ratio</sub>
- **Pre-concentrate dilute isopropanol (about 31 wt%) before extractive dehydration. When: fermentation broth, preconcentration, derived optimum. <sub>jankovic-2023-ipa-acetone-recovery.preconcentrate-before-extractive</sub>
- **Pick an extractive solvent that boils well above the mixture, is thermally stable, easy to recover and of low toxicity. When: solvent choice. <sub>li-2017-ed-thermo-parameters.extractive-solvent-criteria</sub>

### heat integration

- **Include reboilers and condensers in the pinch analysis, and place each column so it sits entirely above or entirely below the pinch.** lead, book or review; Ali et al. 2022, Pinch analysis of the full system, p. 15. When: pinch analysis, column placement, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>ali-2022-eg-plant-pinch.columns-in-pinch-analysis</sub>
- **Place heat engines such as steam turbines to reject heat below the pinch; in this plant that reduced external cooling by about another 6%.** lead, book or review; Ali et al. 2022, Conclusion, p. 19 (grand composite curve). When: pinch analysis, steam turbine, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>ali-2022-eg-plant-pinch.heat-engine-below-pinch</sub>
- **Integrate the surplus heat of the exothermic ethylene oxidation with the energy-hungry glycol dehydration and separation section; in this plant the retrofit targets cut external heating by about 93% and cooling by about 45%.** lead, book or review; Ali et al. 2022, Conclusion, p. 19. When: ethylene glycol plant, retrofit, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>ali-2022-eg-plant-pinch.integrate-eo-reactor-with-glycol-section</sub>
- **Never transfer heat across the pinch, which costs twice in utilities; at the pinch, match streams so the hot stream's heat-capacity flow is no larger than the cold one's above the pinch and no smaller below it.** lead, book or review; Ali et al. 2022, Heat exchanger network rules, p. 16. When: pinch analysis, network design, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>ali-2022-eg-plant-pinch.no-transfer-across-pinch</sub>
- **A heat pump pays when reboiler duty divided by compressor work exceeds about 10 and does not below about 5, which is why heat pumps suit close-boiling columns with a small top-bottom temperature difference.** lead, book or review; Blahušiak et al. 2018, Heat pumps, p. 313 (Fig. 15). When: heat pump. <sub>blahusiak-2018-separation-selection.heat-pump-criterion</sub>
- **For dilute recovery the authors minimise external energy as the design objective, because operating cost dominates capital except for very short payback periods.** lead, book or review; Janković et al. 2023, Methods, p. 715. When: fermentation broth, objective choice. <sub>jankovic-2023-ipa-acetone-recovery.minimise-energy-as-cost-proxy</sub>
- **Apply mechanical vapour recompression to a column whose top and bottom temperatures are close; it pays when its coefficient of performance (8.8 for the vacuum column) clearly exceeds the electricity-to-heat factor (2.5 assumed).** lead, book or review; Janković et al. 2023, Results, Vacuum distillation, p. 717; Methods, p. 716. When: fermentation broth, mechanical vapour recompression. <sub>jankovic-2023-ipa-acetone-recovery.mvr-when-temperatures-close</sub>
- **Do not use vapour recompression on columns with a wide top-to-bottom temperature span, such as the extractive and solvent-recovery columns. Use the hot recovered solvent to boil part of the extractive column's bottoms instead (16-17% less external heat).** lead, book or review; Janković et al. 2023, Results, Recovery of high-purity products, p. 720. When: fermentation broth, extractive distillation, solvent recovery. <sub>jankovic-2023-ipa-acetone-recovery.no-mvr-wide-temperature-span</sub>
- **The vacuum overhead becomes a subcooled liquid after pumping to atmospheric pressure. Preheating it with hot water bottoms or hot solvent cut the acetone column's reboiler duty by 12-41%.** lead, book or review; Janković et al. 2023, Results, Recovery of high-purity products, p. 721. When: fermentation broth, feed preheat. <sub>jankovic-2023-ipa-acetone-recovery.preheat-subcooled-feed</sub>
- **Which configuration wins depends on the heat-to-electricity price ratio: cheap heat favours multi-effect desorption, cheap electricity the heat-pump designs.** lead, book or review; Janković et al. 2023, Results, Economic evaluation, p. 722. When: fermentation broth, utility prices, heat pump vs multi effect. <sub>jankovic-2023-ipa-acetone-recovery.price-ratio-decides-configuration</sub>
- **Feeding the first column's distillate as vapour, without condensing it, to the heteroazeotropic column cut that column's reboiler duty by about 59% (163 against 402 kW) in the 1,4-dioxane case.** lead, book or review; Kruber & Skiborowski 2022, Section 3.3, p. 16 (Fig. 11). When: heteroazeotropic distillation, vapour feed, dioxane benzene case. <sub>kruber-skiborowski-2022-heteroazeotropic-init.vapour-distillate-feed</sub>
- **Without heat integration, thermally coupled complex columns beat sequences of simple columns by a wide margin; once heat integration is included the difference narrows a lot.** lead, book or review; Li et al. 2023, Abstract, p. 1. When: thermally coupled. <sub>li-2023-distillation-sequences.coupled-columns-vs-heat-integration</sub>
- **Pinch-based heat integration of biodiesel plants cut heating and cooling utilities by roughly 11 to 16% in the cited studies.** lead, book or review; Pasha et al. 2021, Section 'Heat integration'. When: pinch analysis. <sub>pasha-2021-biodiesel-process-design.pinch-savings-biodiesel</sub>
- **Carbonation of ethylene oxide is strongly exothermic, and the paper uses the heat removed from the carbonate reactors to raise low-pressure steam.** lead, book or review; Shehata et al. 2024, Section 'MEG production via indirect EO hydration process', pp. 7-8. When: ethylene carbonate route, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>shehata-2024-meg-routes.carbonation-heat-to-steam</sub>

When: direct hydration, multi effect evaporation, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>shehata-2024-meg-routes.evaporator-train-before-vacuum-column</sub>

- **Raising the acetic acid to n-butanol feed ratio raises butanol conversion in the membrane reactor, but the authors keep 1:1 because the excess acid makes product purification harder.** lead, book or review; Al-Rabiah et al. 2022, Section 4, p. 6 (Fig. 5b); Table 3, p. 8. - **For water-removal membranes, zeolite-coated ceramics (LTA or MFI type) withstand heat and chemicals better than polymer films. - **The required purity can change the best technology: for isobutanol at 98.8 wt% pervaporation ranked above azeotropic distillation, while at 99.9 wt% distillation-assisted pervaporation with heat integration was clearly best.** lead, book or review; Valentini & Vaccaro 2020, Section 2.4. ### pfr

- **In the conventional fixed-bed reactor over Amberlyst-15 at 363 K and a 1:1 feed, n-butanol conversion levels off at about 70% (69.8%) within roughly 2.5 m of bed. When: kinetics, amberlyst 15, 363 k, derived by lab, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>al-rabiah-2022.kinetic-laws-imply-different-keq</sub>
- **The conventional glycol reactor is an adiabatic tube in turbulent flow without back-mixing, fed with oxide diluted in a large water excess. When: direct hydration, adiabatic, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>othman-2024-meg-reactive-distillation.tubular-reactor-no-backmixing</sub>
- **In non-catalytic hydration of ethylene oxide, a large water excess (10 to 25 mol per mol oxide cited, 10 simulated) suppresses di- and triethylene glycol. ### pressure swing distillation

- **For tetrahydrofuran + water, pressure-swing distillation showed better controllability than extractive distillation, whose added solvent and longer time constants complicate control.** lead, book or review; Mtogo et al. 2021, Conclusions. - **Pressure-swing distillation needs an azeotrope whose composition moves with pressure and adds no solvent. ### reactive distillation

- **The paper's reactive column has 34 stages, catalyst on stages 5-24, acetic acid fed on stage 5 above n-butanol on stage 9 (100 kmol/h each). - **Reactive distillation needed the least steam (26,388 MWh/a) and the lowest capital (6.7 million USD against 7.6 million for the membrane route) with a payback of 2.1 years. The authors note its design and operation are complex.** lead, book or review; Al-Rabiah et al. 2022, Section 1, p. 2; Section 7.1, p. 16 (Table 10); Section 8, p. 18 (Table 12). When: route choice, economics, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>al-rabiah-2022.rd-lower-capex-and-energy</sub>
- **With water removed during the reaction, the review reports n-butyl acetate yields rising from about 70% to up to 95% using acidic ionic-liquid catalysts.** lead, book or review; Hoff & Eisenacher 2025, Section 6.1 (citing ref. 174). When: esterification, ionic liquid catalyst, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>hoff-eisenacher-2025-esterification-review.butyl-acetate-yield-with-water-removal</sub>
- **Choose an acid resin by its temperature limit: the review gives about 140 C for Amberlyst 15 and up to 190 C for Amberlyst 70. When: ion exchange resin, esterification, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>hoff-eisenacher-2025-esterification-review.resin-temperature-limit</sub>
- **Put the reactive zone where reactant concentrations are highest. Estimate the non-reactive stages with Fenske-type shortcuts and the reactive stages from the reactive height over the catalytic packing's HETP.** lead, book or review; Kiss et al. 2024, Heuristic approaches, journal p. 1268 (p. 7 of the TU Delft copy; guidelines of Subawalla and Fair). When: first sizing, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>kiss-2024-rd-conceptual-methods.first-sizing</sub>
- **For reactions with a large heat effect, integrate energy between the reactive and separating sections; for slow, strongly endothermic reactions with small equilibrium constants also integrate mass with the stripping section. For thermally neutral reactions mass integration alone suffices.** lead, book or review; Kiss et al. 2024, Synthesis procedures, journal p. 1277 (p. 16 of the TU Delft copy; procedure of Huang et al.). When: internal integration, bears on ethylene glycol, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>kiss-2024-rd-conceptual-methods.heat-effect-integration</sub>
- **Place the reactive section so distillation carries a reaction product out of the liquid, which lifts the equilibrium limit, and, where azeotropes exist, so the reaction prevents the azeotrope from forming.** lead, book or review; Kiss et al. 2024, Journal p. 1270 (p. 9 of the TU Delft copy). When: reactive zone location, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>kiss-2024-rd-conceptual-methods.locate-reactive-section</sub>
- **A reactive column can run neat (stoichiometric feeds) or with 10 to 20% excess of one reactant, which then needs a recovery column. When: feed ratio, controllability, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>kiss-2024-rd-conceptual-methods.neat-versus-excess-feed</sub>
- **Reactive distillation is feasible only where the temperature and pressure windows of the reaction, the catalyst and the separation overlap. ### recycle

- **In the membrane-reactor route one column returns its distillate (about 9 kmol/h each of butanol and acid, with about 1 kmol/h each of ester and water) to the feed vessel. The small recycle reflects the 92% conversion.** lead, book or review; Al-Rabiah et al. 2022, Section 5, p. 7; Table 4, p. 9 (streams 3 and 5). When: membrane route, bears on butyl acetate. <sub>al-rabiah-2022.membrane-route-single-column-recycle</sub>
- **Recycle the distillates of downstream columns to an upstream column so an intermediate impurity (ethanol here) does not accumulate at their tops; the recycle rate has an optimum, since too little lets the impurity into the product and too much costs energy.** lead, book or review; Chen et al. 2018, Methods: 'Recycling the distillates'; Conclusions. When: intermediate impurity. <sub>chen-2018-abe-distillation.recycle-distillate-against-build-up</sub>
- **Design in Douglas's order: batch or continuous, then the input-output structure, the recycle structure, the separation system and finally energy integration.** lead, book or review; Larsson & Skogestad 2000, Section 5, p. 227. When: conceptual design order. <sub>larsson-skogestad-2000-plantwide.douglas-hierarchy</sub>
- **Luyben's recommendation, as reported by the authors: fix one flow in each liquid recycle loop to avoid the snowball effect.** lead, book or review; Larsson & Skogestad 2000, Sections 5 and 6, pp. 228 and 230. When: reactor separator recycle, liquid phase, bears on ethylene glycol. Disagrees with another row here. <sub>larsson-skogestad-2000-plantwide.fix-a-recycle-flow</sub>
- **For liquid-phase reactors the authors keep the reactor hold-up at its maximum, which maximises conversion per pass and minimises recycle; fixing the recycle flow instead carries an economic penalty.** lead, book or review; Larsson & Skogestad 2000, Section 6, p. 230. When: reactor separator recycle, liquid phase, bears on ethylene glycol. Disagrees with another row here. <sub>larsson-skogestad-2000-plantwide.keep-reactor-full</sub>
- **Design from the reactor outwards: choose reactor and catalyst first, then add separations and recycles, because the reaction step sets the purity reached and how hard the purification will be.** lead, book or review; Pasha et al. 2021, Section 'Process design and simulation'. When: conceptual design order. <sub>pasha-2021-biodiesel-process-design.design-from-reactor-outwards</sub>
- **In the ethylene carbonate route the carbon dioxide taken up in carbonation is set free again in hydrolysis. It is separated, compressed and recycled to carbonation, with only a small make-up for losses.** lead, book or review; Shehata et al. 2024, Section 'Indirect hydration process', p. 7; 'MEG production via indirect EO hydration process', p. 8 (Fig. 6). When: ethylene carbonate route, bears on ethylene glycol. <sub>shehata-2024-meg-routes.carbonate-route-co2-recycle</sub>
